[bchliu] Depends on what you are using it for. the MBP will be better as an "all rounder" machine with tons of support and software. The RTX Spark is much quicker in AI with native CUDA support and pretty much every AI app/API is optimised for NVidia platforms to begin with.
[Yve] Not really though? If you're just running Local LLM there's not really that big of an advantage in using Nvidia over Apple or AMD in most general use cases as ROCm and Vulkan support exists. You'll need to look into whatever niche purpose that having a Nvidia card will fulfill for your use case bc in most cases… Yes it's smarter to buy AMD or Apple.
I'm viewing this in the context of Local LLM and not general AI use as well. A portable LLM machine is kind of a joke, there are multiple ways to remote into a pc or the output of your machine if you really need to access it and I'd rather not deal with the potential risks of my laptop dying bc I spilled water on it while in Business/First Class and coincidentally flying over a region Inflight wifi cannot be accessed therefore I'd need this device.
Frankly this product seems like its for business executives to dip their toes into AI while justifying an expensive business laptop and its tax write offs. For some, it's a pretty decent ARM laptop and for others it's just an upgrade from their existing RTX Blackwell Pro laptops.
